claims.text: ALD deposition of Pt on ceria-zirconia will promote atomically dispersed Pt sites rather than aggregated Pt nanoparticles.
ALD-prepared atomically dispersed Pt on ceria-zirconia will improve catalytic activity relative to conventionally impregnated Pt nanoparticles on ceria-zirconia.
ALD-prepared atomically dispersed Pt on ceria-zirconia will improve catalyst durability relative to conventionally impregnated Pt nanoparticles.
The ALD-prepared catalyst can achieve improved performance while using less Pt.
Atomically dispersed Pt provides greater surface-atom availability than aggregated Pt nanoparticles.
Atomically dispersed Pt has stronger interaction with the ceria-zirconia support than aggregated Pt nanoparticles.
Atomic dispersion increases the effective catalytic surface area per Pt atom.
Increasing effective catalytic surface area per Pt atom enhances catalytic activity at lower Pt loadings.
Strong interaction between isolated Pt atoms and ceria-zirconia improves thermal stability.
Strong interaction between isolated Pt atoms and ceria-zirconia increases resistance to Pt sintering.
Improved thermal stability and resistance to sintering increase catalyst durability.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will have higher catalytic conversion efficiency than the impregnated catalyst.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will retain activity better over extended thermal and redox cycling than the impregnated catalyst.
The predicted benefits should hold under automotive-relevant temperatures, gas compositions, and redox cycling.
The predicted benefits may fail when ALD parameters are not optimized or exhaust conditions lie substantially outside the typical operating range.
